episodes.180470: With a shortwave passing through the area and increased atmospheric moisture, numerous thunderstorms developed over Middle Tennessee on July 8, 2023. Some of these thunderstorms briefly became severe with damaging winds noted with a few reports of downed trees. Heavy rain was also reported with these thunderstorms with a report of minor flooding received from Portland.
episodes.180471: Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain in southeastern Pennsylvania on the afternoon and early evening of July 8.  Rainfall totals were as high as 1 to 2 inches.
episodes.180472: Severe storms producing large hail and flash flooding occurred in the Nebraska Panhandle on 8 July 2023.
episodes.180473: Severe storms developed the afternoon and evening of 8 July 2023 and impacted areas across the southeast Wyoming plains.
episodes.180487: During the early morning hours of July 8th two clusters of storms moved across central Indiana with prolific lightning and an isolated gust of wind in Rushville. Several lightning strikes caused fires across Indiana.
episodes.180546: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.180639: Daytime heating led to scattered thunderstorms, some of which reached severe limits.
episodes.181263: An upper level high pressure system over El Paso was being partially suppressed by a short wave moving across northern New Mexico on the evening of the seventh. Scattered thunderstorms developed along a surface pressure trough near the Texas/New Mexico state line and drifted eastward during the late afternoon and evening hours as a broken line of thunderstorms. Hot and dry near surface conditions allowed for high cloud bases supporting severe wind gusts underneath thunderstorm activity. Several Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet sites measured severe wind gusts with the strongest activity.
episodes.181285: A supercell thunderstorm developed across northwestern Weston County and moved south-southeast across western portions of the county. Large hail around golf ball size was reported.
episodes.181286: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over the central Black Hills, producing quarter sized hail north of Sheridan Lake.
episodes.181420: An isolated severe thunderstorm cell moved southward across the Ozark foothills during the late evening hours. Strong winds brought down tree limbs in the path of the storm. The storm occurred near a weak stationary front that extended from the Ozark Mountains east to western Kentucky.
episodes.181422: A cluster of severe thunderstorms moved southward across the Ozark foothills during the overnight hours. Isolated wind damage accompanied the storms in forested hilly terrain. The storms occurred near a weak stationary front that extended from the Ozark Mountains east to western Kentucky.
episodes.181710: Westerly flow and a warm, unstable airmass triggered strong to isolated severe pulse storms during the afternoon and evening when sea breezes and boundaries collided. Storms drifted toward the Atlantic coast into the early evening.
episodes.181711: Westerly flow and a warm, unstable airmass triggered strong to isolated severe pulse storms during the afternoon and evening when sea breezes and boundaries collided. Storms drifted toward the Atlantic coast into the early evening.
episodes.181872: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced localized wind damage in Greene and Madison Counties during the early evening hours.
episodes.181979: A lone waterspout was sighted offshore near North Myrtle Beach.
episodes.182166: On the morning of the 7th, a robust mesoscale convective system (MCS) entered portions of northwestern Oklahoma and translated towards central Oklahoma through mid-morning hours. A corridor of wind damage and one tornado occurred across Woodward County due to a mesovortex. Elsewhere, intermittent increases in storm intensity lead to reports and measurements of severe-caliber wind and small hail. Brief training of heavy thunderstorm cores also lead to street flooding near the community of Kingfisher.||During the evening hours of the 7th, an additional MCS developed across the Texas Panhandle and entered western Oklahoma. Once again, wind damage occurred with the most intense portions of the thunderstorm line. This included a report of extensive wind damage near Foss State Park in Custer County.
episodes.182310: A Piedmont trough was the focus of initially isolated thunderstorms during the mid afternoon. The storms formed over the eastern Piedmont, then became more clustered as they moved southeast and south through portions of Edgecombe, Wilson, Franklin, Wake, Wilson, Nash, Wayne, Harnett, Johnston, and Sampson Counties.
episodes.182957: In the middle afternoon, storms began forming in northeastern Colorado. As the day progresses, a line of storm cells formed with one cell producing multiple wind gusts around 100 MPH based on the tree damage left behind.  These storms also produced hail up to quarter in size.  Flash flooding occurred in St. Francis due to the accumulating hail and heavy rainfall causing Highway 36 to become impassable for a short time.
episodes.182970: In the middle afternoon, storms began forming in northeastern Colorado. As the day progresses, a line of storm cells formed with one cell producing hail up to 4 inches and wind gusts estimated up to 80 MPH.
episodes.182973: A surface trough over the central North Carolina Piedmont coupled with an upper trough led to scattered thunderstorm development that eventually merged into a line of showers and thunderstorms over the northwest Piedmont. These storms tracked east into the Triangle, Sandhills, and Coastal Plain by late in the evening hours, weakening with eastward extent into the overnight hours. Flash flooding was reported in Alamance and Wake counties.
episodes.182983: A mid level trough brought good instability and deep moisture leading to localized flash flooding in Connecticut on the evening of the 8th.
episodes.182984: A mid level trough brought good instability and deep moisture leading to localized flash flooding in western Massachusetts on the evening of the 8th.
episodes.182991: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.182997: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.183011: Thunderstorms developed along and ahead of an approaching cold front during the early morning hours of the 8th, and moved into southeastern Oklahoma during the morning hours. The strongest storm produced damaging wind in Le Flore County.
episodes.183063: During the late afternoon of the 7th a line of thunderstorms developed in eastern New Mexico and proceeded to move east into and across the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles. The strongest and most severe of these storms mainly impacted the TX Panhandle as it progressed. Several severe wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph winds were measured by ground stations across the area. Some of the strongest parts of the storms even produced some heavy rainfall.
episodes.183343: Almost three inches of rain dumped in Monticello (Drew County) on the 6th, and high water flowed across Highway 278. The road had to be closed temporarily. It was the same story at Greenbrier (Faulkner County), with numerous roads under water.
episodes.183411: Typical summertime thunderstorms produced some minor wind damage, localized flooding, and two injuries due to lightning.
episodes.183531: A strong to severe storm dropped over five inches of rain in a 2-hour time period on the southeast side of Springfield during the late afternoon. This led to flash flooding along Galloway Creek, and tree damage due to winds estimated in excess of 50 mph.
episodes.183631: Clusters of strong thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast Georgia and southeast South Carolina during the afternoon and early evening hours. These thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the coast.
episodes.183633: Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of a surface trough in the afternoon hours and eventually tracked toward the east. These thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the southeast Georgia and southeast South Carolina coast.
episodes.183767: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with low pressure and a surface trough produced damaging winds across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.183773: Scattered thunderstorms associated with low pressure and a surface trough produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central and southeast Virginia.
episodes.183774: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with low pressure and a surface trough produced damaging winds across portions of southeast Virginia.
episodes.183776: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail and intense winds over parts of the urban corridor and northeast plains and included:  Adams, Arapahoe, Denver, Elbert, Jefferson, Lincoln, Phillips and Weld counties.  The hail ranged in size from 1 to 2 inches in diameter, with peak wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph.  In addition, heavy rain flooded an underpass along Highway 36, with 3 feet of standing water which closed the roadway for several hours.
episodes.183861: A low pressure area aloft over the eastern United States contributed to instability which led to the development of a few strong thunderstorms along the Palm Beach County coast.
episodes.183966: Isolated thunderstorms developed over western North Carolina during the afternoon. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Charlotte. This storm also moved very slowly and produced torrential rainfall.
episodes.184000: A weak cold front extended from West Tennessee into central Arkansas during the afternoon hours on July 8, 2023. This front was moving slowly south. This feature combined with strong instability and deep moisture resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms across the Mid-South. Isolated wind damage and flash flooding occurred.
episodes.184001: A weak cold front extended from West Tennessee into central Arkansas during the afternoon hours on July 8, 2023. This front was moving slowly south. This feature combined with strong instability and deep moisture resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms across the Mid-South. Isolated wind damage and flash flooding occurred.
episodes.184061: A hot and humid summertime environment triggered pulse storms to form over southern Mississippi and southeast Louisiana. Different clusters formed throughout the afternoon and moved over the marine areas.
episodes.184126: Residual moisture from an incredibly anomalously wet June continues to moisten the lower levels aiding in ample amounts of instability. The northwest flow pattern created a lot of shear, which led to prolonged 3 day severe weather event over adjacent and eastern plains of southern Colorado.
episodes.184239: A front moved across Interior Alaska on July 7, 2023 bringing numerous thunderstorms to the Interior. Many of the storms were far longer lasting than typical Interior Alaska thunderstorms. Radar signatures suggested several storms produced large hail and strong winds over a large, but mostly unpopulated area.
episodes.184286: A warm front was across portions of southeast Missouri. With plenty of instability, moisture and lift near the boundary, several strong to severe storms developed in this area. There were several reports of damaging winds and large hail.
episodes.184306: Thunderstorms developed and moved slowly southward through Eastern North Carolina during the evening hours. One such storm became severe and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184422: Showers and thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a surface cold front which gradually moved through southern Indiana and central Kentucky during the evening hours of July 8th, 2023. With instability values ranging between 2000-2500 J/kg and 35-40 knots of effective bulk shear, the parameter space was favorable for a few strong to severe storms. Ultimately, only isolated wind damage was observed in the vicinity of a few stronger storms along the Ohio River, with localized wind damage being observed in Jefferson and Oldham County, Kentucky.
episodes.184423: Heavy rain brought flooding to the Cache River at Patterson in early July.
